# Dataset


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

The dataset is the lasting artifact of the [scope](design/scope.ipynb):
every model is rebuilt from a version of it. Each version is a JSON
Lines file under `data/`, committed with the code that made it, and
never overwritten. A training file holds one line for each record and
teacher. The test file holds the records only, because the code checks
score a message against its record.

## Files

[`write_jsonl`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/dataset.html#write_jsonl)
and
[`read_jsonl`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/dataset.html#read_jsonl)
write and read one JSON object per line, keeping non-ASCII text such as
farm names and emoji readable:

## Records

[`records`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/dataset.html#records)
samples `n` records with
[`sample`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/synth.html#sample)
and gives each an id from its seed and position, such as `s4-0017`.
Records also found in `exclude`, such as the test set, are dropped, so
no test input is ever used for training:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/franckalbinet/edgeslm/blob/main/edgeslm/dataset.py#L36"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### records

``` python
def records(
    n:int, # Number of records to sample
    seed:int, # Seed of the sample
    exclude:list=(), # Rows whose records must not appear
)->list: # Dicts with `id`, `tuple` and `record`
```

*`n` sampled records with ids, minus any in `exclude`*

## The frozen test set

The test set used to be regenerated from seed 1, so every change to the
generator changed it. It is now written once, and read from its file
from then on. This cell made it, and does not run in tests:

``` python
write_jsonl('../data/test-v1.jsonl', records(270, seed=1))
```

It holds 10 records for each of the 27 tuples:

``` python
test = read_jsonl('../data/test-v1.jsonl')
test_eq(set(Counter(tuple(r['tuple'].values()) for r in test).values()), {10})
len(test), test[0]['id']
```

    (270, 's1-0000')

## Teacher messages

[`label`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/dataset.html#label)
has a teacher write the message for one record and runs the code checks
on it. A message that fails is written again once, with the failed
checks’ failure modes added to the prompt. The row keeps the second
attempt and its checks either way, so that failures can be counted and
left out of training.
[`label_all`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/dataset.html#label_all)
runs every record through every teacher, a few calls at a time to stay
within rate limits:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/franckalbinet/edgeslm/blob/main/edgeslm/dataset.py#L64"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### label_all

``` python
async def label_all(
    rows:list, # Rows from `records`
    models:list, # Teacher models
    n_workers:int=8, # Calls at a time
)->list: # One labelled row per record and model
```

*Label every row with every model*

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### label

``` python
async def label(
    row:dict, # A row from `records`
    model:str='claude-haiku-4-5', # Teacher model
)->dict: # `row` with the message, its checks, the attempt number and the provenance
```

*Have `model` write and check the message for `row`*

This cell wrote the first training set: 200 records from seed 4, each
labelled by Haiku and Sonnet. It needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the
untracked `.env` file, and does not run in tests:

``` python
from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv()
rows = records(200, seed=4, exclude=test)
write_jsonl('../data/train-v1.jsonl', await label_all(rows, ['claude-haiku-4-5', 'claude-sonnet-4-6']))
```

Each record has one row per teacher, and every row was written with the
same prompt:

``` python
train = read_jsonl('../data/train-v1.jsonl')
test_eq(set(Counter(r['id'] for r in train).values()), {2})
test_eq(len({r['prompt'] for r in train}), 1)
len(train), train[0]['prompt']
```

    (400, '3ec23e301454')

Almost every message passed the checks at the first attempt. Each
teacher has one message that is still too long after the second attempt,
and is left out of training:

``` python
Counter((r['model'], r['attempt'], all(r['checks'].values())) for r in train)
```

    Counter({('claude-haiku-4-5', 1, True): 199,
             ('claude-sonnet-4-6', 1, True): 198,
             ('claude-haiku-4-5', 2, False): 1,
             ('claude-sonnet-4-6', 2, True): 1,
             ('claude-sonnet-4-6', 2, False): 1})

The two teachers often write the same message. The rules and examples
leave little room for wording, so a comparison of teachers would measure
almost nothing, and the student trains on Haiku’s messages, as the
scope’s Choice of teacher section decides:

``` python
msgs = {(r['id'], r['model']): r['message'].strip() for r in train}
ids = sorted({r['id'] for r in train})
sum(msgs[i, 'claude-haiku-4-5'] == msgs[i, 'claude-sonnet-4-6'] for i in ids), len(ids)
```

    (73, 200)
